title: Fit a power law on log paper and extrapolate it
brief: Evaluate a power law, recover its exponent and coefficient with a least-squares line in log space, and use the fit to predict a size you never measured.
hints: power_law_eval is one line: c * x**k. Turn x into an array first with np.asarray(x, dtype=float) so a Python list works.

fit_power_law works on logs: u = np.log(x), v = np.log(y). Subtract each mean, then k = sum(uc * vc) / sum(uc**2). The intercept is v.mean() - k * u.mean(), and c is np.exp of that intercept, not the intercept itself.
extrapolate fits first, then evaluates the fitted law at x_new. Reuse the two functions you already wrote.
